digest.component_or_area: Jira write dispatch and retry orchestration
propositions: Jira writes currently cross multiple independent retry layers (generic dispatch, Cloud ACLI/REST, DC SDK/wrapper), causing ambiguous outcomes on timeout and potential write multiplication.

A provider-neutral operation/outcome contract with exact logical id, stable postcondition, bounded invocation/sleep budget (max 3 invocations, 15 seconds cumulative), and deterministic recovery strategy is required to disambiguate write success.

Cloud and DC summary-write routes must be selected via constructor-injected internal executor selector (defaulting to legacy, no config/env surface) and execute exactly one logical operation without dual-send or generic retry.

DC summary writes must execute exactly GET→PUT→GET per invocation with no hidden repeats; Cloud ACLI recovery must use one primary-store REST GET with no sleep, and observation of desired state post-timeout proves recovered success.

Terminal outcomes must emit exactly one redacted per-mutation completion log (max 512 Unicode per message, 1024 total) containing logical id, disposition, invocation/request counts, cleanup status, retry_not_before, and message; S1 records error/disposition without deferral or baseline advance, leaving bridge consumption to S3.
